person.persName: dri ma med pa'i bshes gnyen

person.note:
His dates can be approximated as 1070-1130.
He is possibly the same person as Byang 'chad khyung (ID:6382), as [NA9AMDH6] states that Khyung rin chen grags held Byang 'chad (ID:4416) and taught Sa chen (ID:4205) there ([647FFPZR]: 543). [CJ75QQKN]: 339 (fol. 8a/170a1-3). dMar ston's Zhib mo rdo rje ([RA3FK3BK]: 134 and 137), on the other hand, distinguish the two figures and places Sa chen's studies with Khyung at Nyang stod byang 'chad, and those with Khyung rin chen grags at Nyang stod.
On the reference to Khyung as "slang pa/slang pha/slang pha ba" (understood as a regionalism for "glang pa/glang pha ba," see [WL39GVT5]: 940.

person.persName: zul phul bya 'dul ba 'dzin pa chen po
person.note: Born in 1091 at gTsang rong gyung and died at the age of 76 in Zul phu according to [R894SIKE]: 109. [W4T5ZMUP]: 38 accordingly proposes the dates 1091-1166. [VKBZTBWN], fol. 3b6 reports that he was born the year rNgog lo (ID:3786) came back to Tibet, i.e., ca. 1092. On his life, based on the Zul phu mkhan byang chub rin chen dpal bzang po'i rnam par thar pa (ID:6715), see [W4T5ZMUP]: 40. It is unclear whether he is the same person as rGya 'dul ba 'dzin pa (ID:4193). The [NA9AMDH6] distinguishes two "rGya 'dul 'dzin" - the elder (ID: 3941) and the younger (ID:4193) - and a "Bya 'dul 'dzin brTson 'grus 'bar" (student of 'Bre chen po). In contrast, the [R894SIKE] only mentions one "rGya 'dul 'dzin" (the elder), distinct from "Bya 'dul 'dzin" (who was ordained by 'Bre). [VKBZTBWN], fol. 6b5-6 and [8VLVHDR2], fol. 14b5 report that he was ordained by 'Bre and received from him the name in religion brTson 'grus 'bar. A number of the same teachers are mentioned for rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger and Bya 'dul 'dzin but, for instance, the latter's studies with rGya 'dul 'dzin the older took place when he was a retired abbot, whereas the former's studies with him took place when he was still abbot. Further, rGya 'dul 'dzin the younger became abbot of dGa' ba sdong and Bya 'dul abbot of Zul phu. This suggests they might have been distinct persons.
Passed away at 36 ([R894SIKE]: 109). According to [W4T5ZMUP]: 40, in 1126.

Native of Nyang stod Mang ra ba (or Mang rab) born in sTag gi rGya ma ra ba in the vicinity of rBa brCad, known as "rGya 'Dul 'dzin the elder" to distinguish him from "rGya 'Dul 'dzin the younger" (ID:4193). See [647FFPZR]: 541. See also [UGZJBIWM]: 376.
Disciple of Zhang zhung pa rGyal ba'i shes rab and Ye shes bla ma in sTod, gZhon tshul in 'Dzims and 'Brom Seng dkar in dBus. His disciples include sTon pa Yang rab from Glo bo, the elder and younger Brag ston in western gTsang, the elder Leng and the younger 'Brog, and 'Gar (=Rong pa 'Gar dGe ba gsal), 'Gos (=rje 'Gos) and Yol (=Yol Chos dbang) ([Q922IUFM]: 1: 98).

person.persName: yar lung pa gzus rdo rje rgyal mtshan
person.note: A disciple of Klu mes (/Gru mer) mentioned in [R894SIKE]: 106.
In view of the references in 'Dul ba'i bslab pa spyir bstan rnam bshad (ID:4708), he was a second-generation student in the lineage of Bya 'dul 'dzin (ID:3818).

bibl.title: 'dul ba'i bslab pa spyir bstan rnam bshad
འདུལ་བའི་བསླབ་པ་སྤྱིར་བསྟན་རྣམ་བཤད
'dul baʼi bslab pa spyir bstan gyi rnam bshad
bibl.author: Anonymous
bibl.note:
Based on the lemmata, this is a commentary on the Pratimokṣa­sūtra­ṭīkā­vinaya­samuccaya (ID:7386), which addresses the portion corresponding to D4106, 129b4 to 142a6. The text does not have a colophon.
The author makes numerous references (in the form "... na re" to the views of "rgya" (presumably rGya 'dul 'dzin (ID:3941)), which he refutes. Also cited are Sog (ID:3940), Khyung rin chen grags (ID:3809), gZus rdo rje rgyal mtshan (ID:6432) and the yet unidentified rKyang 'dul gar ston (ID:8637). Ten references in the form "bya'i zhal nas" (for views that are not criticized) presumably refer to Bya 'dul 'dzin brtson 'grus 'bar (ID:3818). Also cited in this form is rMa tsho (ID:3942), Bya 'dul 'dzin's teacher, and "rtsis pa," presumably Bya 'dul's student gZhon nu seng ge (ID:3946), "rong pa" (maybe Bya 'dul's student gTsang rong pa lCe 'dul 'dzin (ID:3947)), and an anonymous "mkhan po chen po."
The author can thus be situated in the lineage of Bya 'dul, probably among his second- or third-generation students.
